candidates.abstract: Memory models specify the behaviors that concurrent programs may exhibit under compiler and hardware optimizations, which often deviate from Sequential Consistency (SC). Robustness is the property of a program P not exhibiting any weak behaviors when executing under a weak memory model MM, compared to SC. As such, the algorithmic problem of deciding whether $P$ is robust against MM has been studied extensively, and has been repeatedly shown to be in PSPACE for many memory models, such as TSO, PSO, and Release/Acquire. However, each model has required its own, dedicated proof, raising the natural question of whether robustness admits a unifying treatment across memory models. In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for a broad class of memory models definable in Kleene Algebra with Tests (KAT). We prove that robustness against any prefix-closed, KAT-definable memory model is in PSPACE. This metatheorem recovers nearly all prior PSPACE robustness results, and establishes PSPACE membership for several new models, including the full RC11 and the OCaml memory model. We have further formalized the correctness of our approach in Lean. On the other hand, we prove that robustness against the KAT-definable Relaxed model is undecidable, and thus prefix-closedness cannot be dropped, in general. Finally, we implement our algorithm in a prototype tool RoboKAT, and demonstrate its flexibility by checking robustness against nine memory models, several of which are not handled by prior work.

contribution.en: Uses a unifying metatheorem to prove PSPACE robustness for any prefix-closed KAT-definable memory model, formalized in Lean, plus undecidability for the relaxed model.
contribution.zh: 用统一元定理证明任意前缀闭 KAT 可定义内存模型的鲁棒性属于 PSPACE，并在 Lean 中形式化，同时给出松弛模型不可判定性。

why_care.en: Memory-model robustness bears on compiler correctness for concurrent code and offers a clean, reusable formal argument.
why_care.zh: 内存模型鲁棒性关系到并发代码的编译正确性，并提供清晰可复用的形式化论证。

candidates.title: A Unifying Metatheorem on Weak-Memory Robustness

candidates.abstract: Definitional interpreters provide an executable and pedagogically effective way to explain programming language semantics. However, when implemented in a dynamically typed and effectful metalanguage, semantic components such as stores, continuations, handlers, substitutions, and scheduling states may remain implicit in the host-language implementation, making it harder to see how language extensions affect interpreter structure. This paper reconstructs the family of interpreters from \textit{Essentials of Programming Languages} (EOPL) in Haskell, a statically typed and purely functional metalanguage, for pedagogical use. We preserve the object languages, examples, and tests of EOPL while making their semantic components explicit through algebraic data types, evaluator signatures, and explicit semantic domains. Across 15 interpreters and 6 type checkers, language extensions are exposed as systematic type-directed changes. The reconstruction is currently used in undergraduate and graduate programming language courses, where students learn interpreter construction through incremental and test-driven development. We further illustrate its pedagogical use through three case studies that progressively extend students' experience: composing mutable state and exception handling, deriving an actor-based interpreter from the typed structure of the EOPL thread interpreter, and translating the CHECKED interpreter and type checker into Rocq to mechanize type safety. Together, the classroom experience and case studies suggest that the reconstruction provides a concrete bridge from learning programming language concepts through executable interpreters to language design and mechanized reasoning.

contribution.en: Reconstructs EOPL's 15 interpreters and 6 type checkers in statically typed, purely functional Haskell, making semantic components explicit for teaching.
contribution.zh: 用静态类型纯函数式 Haskell 重构 EOPL 的 15 个解释器和 6 个类型检查器，使语义组件显式化并服务教学。

why_care.en: Weakly connected to compiler optimization, IR, GPU, and PIM work; only indirectly useful for semantics pedagogy and mechanized reasoning.
why_care.zh: 与编译器优化、IR、GPU 和 PIM 等主线关联很弱，仅对语言语义教学和机械化证明有间接价值。

candidates.title: Statically Typed Purely Functional Definitional Interpreters for {\it Essentials of Programming Languages}

recommendations.abstract: Efficient execution on modern parallel machines requires more than abundant parallelism; it demands instruction coherence, memory coherence, and load balance to maximize SIMD utilization and memory bandwidth. Efficiently mapping \textit{divergent} parallel workloads to modern machines, where control flow, memory accesses, and unbounded iteration depend on per-thread runtime values, often requires global program restructuring that trades off increased coherence with reduced locality, parallelism, or extra work. We observe that the key optimizations used to accelerate divergent parallel programs can be expressed as compositions of well-known program transformations from the functional programming and loop optimization communities. We operationalize this insight through \textit{parallel dispatch graphs}: a compilation model that represents divergent programs by representing control flow, data flow between logical stages, and parallel loops within a single abstraction. To facilitate rapid exploration of points in the optimization space, we provide a scheduling language that includes composable transformations of data-dependent control flow and data flow, together with standard loop transformations and hardware bindings. This separation of concerns allows the core algorithm to remain portable, while the execution schedule can be specialized to the specifics of target hardware and input data values. We evaluate our system using popular applications from the domain of spatial computing, and show that the optimization strategies of hand-optimized parallel tree traversals, path tracers, and Monte Carlo PDE solvers can be reproduced as schedules in our system. Our generated code matches or outperforms the hand-optimized implementations (geomeans $1.02$--$2.95\times$ faster). Additionally, we demonstrate empirically that the best schedule varies across programs, machines, and inputs.

contribution.en: Introduces parallel dispatch graphs and a composable scheduling language to express control-flow, data-flow, and loop transformations for divergent parallel programs.
contribution.zh: 提出并行调度图这一编译模型，并用可组合调度语言统一表达发散程序的控制流、数据流和并行循环变换。

why_care.en: Directly informs scheduling-language and IR design for improving instruction and memory coherence in divergent workloads while preserving portability.
why_care.zh: 与调度语言、IR和SIMD/GPU代码生成直接相关，可用于在保持可移植性的同时提升发散负载的指令与内存一致性。

recommendations.title: A Compilation Model for Divergent Parallel Workloads

recommendations.abstract: For automatic optimization systems, performance portability across increasingly diverse AI accelerators remains a challenge. We investigate how well graph-level superoptimization transfers across architectures by adapting Mirage from its CUDA-oriented design to the Huawei Ascend 910B3 through a Triton-based compilation stack. We evaluate the adapted system on transformer-relevant workloads, including matrix multiplication, softmax, RMSNorm+MatMul, gated MLP, FNN, and attention. The results show that graph-level optimization can successfully transfer and outperform available reference implementations by up to 87.0% on fused workloads. However, performance is highly dependent on tensor shape and workload structure, with substantial regressions for other configurations. We identify target-specific tensor partitioning, execution-resource modeling, backend lowering and fusion, and search and verification costs as key limitations. Our findings demonstrate that a portable graph representation and programming model do not imply a portable optimization space, motivating modular target-specific mechanisms within otherwise reusable compiler infrastructure.

contribution.en: Adapts the Mirage tensor-graph superoptimizer to an Ascend NPU through Triton and empirically studies how well graph-level optimization transfers across architectures.
contribution.zh: 将Mirage张量图超优化器经Triton移植到昇腾NPU，并系统评估图级优化的跨架构可迁移性。

why_care.en: Shows that a portable graph representation does not imply a portable optimization space, so retargetable superoptimizers need target-specific partitioning, cost modeling, and lowering.
why_care.zh: 表明可移植的图表示并不等于可移植的优化空间，提示可重定向超优化器需要目标特定的划分、代价建模与后端下沉。

recommendations.title: How well does graph superoptimization transfer? Adapting tensor-graph superoptimizer to a Triton-based NPU
